Presentation also needs attention.","next_steps":["Correct the Orbit section: remove or properly justify the RAAN of 27.33° against Kourou's longitude, and revise the sunlight claim to account for eclipse seasons in your sun-synchronous orbit.","Remove the duplicated access 15 row, recalculate the mean and total access times, and revisit your altitude argument so it is consistent with your imaging-quality requirement.","Complete the End-of-Life section: finish the truncated drag-sail sentence, quantify orbital lifetime at 600 km, and assess the drag-sail and graveyard options. Errors limit the rating: the RAAN justification is incorrect, access 15 duplicates access 14 and skews the statistics, and the drag-sail sentence is incomplete. Wikipedia sources and an unflown Vega E weaken the launch plan. Adding hand calculations and STK files would strengthen the evidence.","C3":"Your conclusion draws the configuration together and notes the launch-vehicle risk and its fallback, which is sensible. It is largely generic, however, restating the design rather than reporting findings such as pass count or contact statistics. The closing claim that the work will hopefully contribute is not backed by the evidence presented. State specific quantitative outcomes and link each to a design decision.","C4":"Your report has a clear structure, with contents, an executive summary and headed sections, which is a good foundation. Presentation is held back by figures and tables that lack numbers (tables also lack captions), incomplete sentences, garbled bibliography entries such as reference [10], and launch citations [49]-[74] missing from the bibliography. Consistent labelling and a reference list that matches your in-text citations would bring this to a professional standard."}}
